links.outcome: Organizational use of steering committees for AI oversight and fragmented governance structures
links.effect: 78.9% of organizations reported using steering committees for AI oversight, some combined with IT, research, or innovation teams; authors conclude organizations lack standardized approaches and rely on fragmented governance.
links.quote: Health care organizations lack standardized approaches to AI safety and often rely on fragmented governance structures.

links.outcome: Barriers to AI implementation including lack of AI expertise
links.effect: Lack of AI expertise reported as a barrier by 68.4% of organizations; difficulty evaluating AI effectiveness by 52.6%.
links.quote: Barriers to AI implementation included interoperability challenges (78.9%), lack of AI expertise (68.4%), and difficulty evaluating AI effectiveness (52.6%).

screen.reason: Qualitative empirical study (semi-structured interviews with 22 health care quality and safety leaders across 19 organizations) assessing organizational readiness, governance structures, and barriers to safe AI integration in actual health systems.
